description: RAVEN (Risk Analysis Virtual Environment) is an open-source framework from Idaho National Laboratory for parametric and probabilistic analysis driven by the response of complex system codes. It was first developed by Cristian Rabiti, Andrea Alfonsi, Joshua Cogliati, Robert Kinoshita and Diego Mandelli for nuclear plant safety work with RELAP-7 on the MOOSE framework, including control logic and dynamic accident scenario evolution. It samples codes with Monte Carlo, grid or Latin hypercube schemes for uncertainty quantification and reliability, finds limit surfaces that separate inputs leading to failure using supervised learning, builds and uses reduced-order surrogate models, and post-processes time-dependent and steady-state results with statistics and sensitivity analysis. The method is location-independent. It is Python code on GitHub, version 3.2, under the Apache 2.0 licence at no cost, with the last commit in July 2026. Caveats: meaningful use needs a coupled system code and considerable setup. Simulation uses are probabilistic risk assessment, reliability analysis and design optimisation of nuclear and energy systems. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
